correctness.rationale: All edge subsets in the labelled rook graph K_m Cartesian K_n have a unique H/V/L component decomposition, proved directly from the third-edge exclusion. Different components must use disjoint row and column supports. Counting labelled supports gives the exact factorial polynomial and two-sort EGF. Support sizes a=t+v≤m and b=t+h≤n prove the maximum and its sole odd-square deficiency; equality cases give exact multiplicities. An independent exhaustive literal third-edge checker confirmed every coefficient for 15 small parameter pairs (852443 valid edge subsets), with exact arithmetic on 261 more profiles; finite computation is not used as an all-order proof.

originality.rationale: The directly related 2022 and 2024 primary articles were read beyond abstracts. They state the general induced-star decomposition or broad graph-product bounds, not a reversible three-block classification with mutually disjoint row/column supports for rook graphs nor the complete two-sort EOP polynomial. Their inequalities do not imply the proved exact coefficient formula, its odd-square parity correction, or optimizer counts. value.rationale: The edge-open packing parameter and general Cartesian product inequalities were already studied, but the complete labelled size enumeration for a natural rook-graph family, including sharp parity-sensitive extremal count and exact multiplicity, supplies a motivated new natural invariant, a reusable two-sort combinatorial decomposition, and stronger structural information than a scalar extremum.
